gen-gf-text-me-one-fs-literata: Text Me One packs its letters in tight as pins in a cushion, with no stroke contrast at all, while Literata's classic serif body adds soft thick-thin shading. Pages read with a bookish, unhurried pull.
gen-gf-thasadith-fs-literata: Thasadith rushes along, its terminals cut open so the shapes flow outward. Literata, a serif with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones, slows everything down into a settled, bookish read.
gen-gf-tillana-bitter: Commanding up top, Tillana stacks a chunky, tall midzone over open-ended curves. Bitter, a slab-serif with a huge lowercase eye and see-through s shapes, makes the grounded, dependable half of the deal.
gen-gf-tillana-inter: Distinctive from the first glance, Tillana has a chunky, tall midzone and open-ended curves. Inter then lays down a smooth, tube-like sans with big counters, so the heading's heft gets a quiet, breathing partner underneath.
gen-gf-tillana-mulish: Tillana's chunky, tall midzone and open-ended curves give the heading its weight, while Mulish stays level like a drafting pen, with no thick-thin modulation. Plain sans against display, they split the work cleanly.
gen-gf-tillana-poppins: Tillana leads with a chunky, tall midzone and open-ended curves that look nothing like anything below. Poppins runs a sans body of single-width strokes, rope-loose curves and sturdy lowercase, so paragraphs stay crisp and modern.
gen-gf-tillana-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab puts a slab-serif body in the middle zone, precise and structured, with open throats on a, c, e and s. And Tillana's chunky, tall midzone gives the heading far more swagger over the paragraphs.
gen-gf-tillana-rubik: Rubik gives lowercase letters that look big beside the capitals, soft and clean, with round shapes that stay readable when small. Tillana's chunky display heading sits above it, so try modest body sizing.
gen-gf-tilt-prism-bitter: Bitter's very large lowercase eye and see-through s make a slab-serif body that feels dependable and grounded over long paragraphs. Tilt Prism, drawn as if with one pen tip, adds a bold display voice up top.
gen-gf-tilt-prism-instrument-sans: Tilt Prism draws each glyph as if with one tip, giving a bold display shout with barely any gap between lowercase and caps. But Instrument Sans does the quiet work, with open pincer-like c ends and strokes that never vary.
